What is microcement?

Think of it as stone-look plaster with no grout lines at all.

Microcement is a thin, cement-based coating troweled on by hand in a few layers, then sealed. It covers walls, floors, showers, and counters as one continuous surface — the look of polished concrete or natural stone, without tiles or grout.

Why it matters in New Orleans: grout is porous, it stays damp, and that's where mold grows. No grout lines means no grout to go black, no re-grouting, and a shower that's easy to wipe down.

And because it's only a few millimeters thick, it can often go right over existing tile once I've confirmed it's solid — less demolition, less mess, less time without a bathroom.

Why Seamless

Built for NOLA humidity —
not generic "wet areas."

No grout, no mold habitat

Grout is porous cement. It absorbs. It holds moisture. That's where mold lives. Seamless surfaces have none.

No joints, no place to sneak behind

Every seam is a chance for water to work its way through. My installs have zero — one continuous surface, wall to floor to niche.

Waterproof for New Orleans, specifically

Not a generic wet-area system. Every material I use is chosen for 76% humidity, foundation shift, and how NOLA houses actually sweat.

What's under the finish

How I waterproof your shower — layer by layer.

The pretty part is the last few millimeters. What keeps water out of your walls is everything underneath — and I'll walk you through every layer for your bathroom before you sign anything.

  1. 01

    Inspect what's really there

    I check the existing tile, backer, slope, and drain, and look for soft spots or hidden water damage before quoting.

  2. 02

    Fix the problems, don't cover them

    Loose tile, rot, or a failed pan gets repaired or rebuilt. Microcement only goes over a solid, stable base.

  3. 03

    Prime and reinforce

    The surface is cleaned, primed, and reinforced so the new layers bond tightly and move with the house.

  4. 04

    Waterproof the wet zone

    A waterproofing layer goes through the shower — corners, niche, bench, and drain detailed so water has nowhere to go.

  5. 05

    Hand-trowel the microcement

    Base and finish coats are troweled on by hand into one continuous surface: no grout, no seams.

  6. 06

    Seal it and show you how to care for it

    Protective sealer coats finish the job. At handoff I explain cleaning and upkeep so it stays looking new.

Straight answers

What people ask before they call.

What is microcement, exactly?

A thin, cement-based coating hand-troweled in layers and sealed. It covers showers, floors, walls, and counters as one continuous surface — the look of polished concrete or stone with no tiles and no grout lines.

Will mold grow on it?

Mold in tile showers lives mostly in grout lines and failing caulk. A sealed microcement shower has no grout lines, so there's no grout for mold to grow in. Like any shower it still needs normal cleaning and ventilation.

Is it really waterproof?

The waterproofing comes from the system underneath and the sealer on top — not from the decorative layer alone. I build the wet zone with a dedicated waterproofing layer and detail the corners, niche, and drain, then seal it. I explain each layer for your bathroom before you sign.

Can it go over my existing tile?

Often, yes — once I've inspected it and confirmed it's solid. If the tile or what's behind it is failing, I'll show you and we'll fix that properly instead of covering a problem.

What does it cost?

Every job is priced individually after a free site visit, because the condition of what's there changes the work. You'll get a written quote with the scope spelled out before you commit to anything.

Do I really get free heated floors?

Yes. Book a whole-bathroom renovation or a whole-floor coating and I buy and install the underfloor heating system at no charge.

Where do you work?

The New Orleans metro — including Metairie, Kenner, Harahan, the Westbank, and St. Bernard — plus the Northshore: Mandeville, Covington, Madisonville, and Slidell.

How does it work from first call to finished?

Call, text, or send the form. I come out for a site visit, you get a written quote, and a deposit locks in your dates. I do the work myself, start to finish.
